answer.question: What should I check before turf goes into a wet Palm Valley yard?
answer.answer: Identify wetland boundaries, existing drainage and the usable part of the property before choosing the turf footprint. Bring rain photos and any property reports. A new surface does not resolve tidal water or a larger drainage problem; any additional assessment or work needs its own scope.

blocks.h2: Choose the area that will change your daily routine.
paras: A lawn beside the patio or a dog area near the door can leave much of a larger property alone. For a green, choose putting lines and a chipping position, then keep paths and ordinary property access around them.

Mark the tree canopy before discussing preparation. Where the applicable Florida standard requires an arborist’s certification for turf beneath the drip line, obtain it before treating that shaded area as available.

blocks.h2: Keep the wetland edge outside an ordinary lawn quote.
paras: Along Palm Valley Road and Roscoe Boulevard, bring any recorded wetland buffer, shoreline or drainage conditions for the actual parcel. Ask the county’s responsible staff about work near those boundaries. A fence or an existing lawn edge does not settle the permitted work area.

Palm Valley and Ponte Vedra Beach share a postal area, but a Palm Valley parcel should not automatically be treated as part of the Ponte Vedra Boulevard zoning district. Confirm the parcel’s requirements and any private covenants. Keep unresolved drainage work separate from the surface estimate.

blocks.h2: The low side of the island, under old oaks.
paras: Palm Valley and Ponte Vedra Beach share a ZIP code, 32082, and little else. Palm Valley is the marsh side of San Pablo Island, east of the Intracoastal and west of A1A, running north from Palm Valley Boulevard to Butler Boulevard, with 12.18 square miles of land and 1.43 of open water (Wikipedia).

Along Palm Valley Road, Roscoe Boulevard and Canal Boulevard, many lots have never been cleared: live oaks, cabbage palms and Spanish moss over the whole yard. If yours stays soft underfoot for days after a storm, and the dog carries the mud inside, the base is the fix, not another round of grass.

On the free visit we look at how your yard drains and what's under it, then build the base to match, so water moves down and away instead of standing in the low corner. The turf goes on top: laid, seamed, edged and finished.

blocks.h2: Often no HOA, and a county code that leaves turf alone.
paras: A large share of Palm Valley, the older acreage strung along Palm Valley Road, Roscoe Boulevard and Canal Boulevard, sits in no HOA at all. That's rare this close to the ocean in St. Johns County. It means no architectural committee, no approval packet and no wait before work starts. Only the gated enclaves have a board to satisfy.

Palm Valley also sits outside the Ponte Vedra Zoning District overlay along Ponte Vedra Boulevard, so the Ponte Vedra zoning board generally isn't your path; St. Johns County is. The county's definition of impervious surface covers compacted materials used for parking or roadways, which a back lawn isn't. Many lots here sit inside wetland buffers that go to the county's natural resources staff (LDC Article IV), so keep the turf's drainage details with your plans.

blocks.h2: No new sod, and nothing to fertilize by the water.
paras: Drinking water comes from the St. Johns County Utility Department, but many of the older acreage properties water their yards from private shallow wells, and near the marsh those wells can pull brackish water.

St. Johns County has been under a Phase III extreme water shortage since 11 May 2026, driven by an extreme drought rating, the highest recorded in Florida since 2000 (St. Johns County). Lawns get one watering day a week, never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., and no new sod or new plantings may go in. If your shaded, soggy lawn gave out this summer, you can't lay sod to replace it while the order stands.

Turf needs no fertilizer, either. The county caps nitrogen at 5 pounds per 1,000 square feet a year and allows none within 10 feet of a surface water body (St. Johns County). On a lot that touches a creek, a canal, the marsh or the Intracoastal, that can rule out a good part of the yard.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Palm Valley, FL?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Palm Valley, FL. Much of the older acreage along Palm Valley Road and Roscoe Boulevard sits in no HOA at all, and a lot that stays wet after a storm needs a base built to drain before anything else. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Do I need HOA approval for turf in Palm Valley?
faq.a: Only if your lot sits in an association, and much of the old acreage doesn't. In gated enclaves such as Marsh Landing Country Club, Sawmill Lakes, Odom's Mill, The Preserve and Isle of Palms, the board still decides what the street or a neighbor can see. Florida law bars it from restricting turf that can't be seen from the frontage, a neighboring lot, a common area or a community golf course (Fla. Stat. 720.3045).

faq.q: I water from my own well. Does the watering order apply to me?
faq.a: Yes. The county's Phase III order covers private wells and pumps as well as utility water (St. Johns County). Odd or unnumbered addresses water on Saturday and even addresses on Sunday, with no more than 3/4 inch and one hour per zone. Drip and micro-spray lines may run at any time.

faq.q: Does state law protect turf on a large Palm Valley parcel?
faq.a: Not automatically. Fla. Stat. 125.572 stops the county banning compliant turf on single-family parcels of one acre or less (Fla. Stat. 125.572), and many acreage parcels here are bigger. The county's Land Development Code doesn't mention artificial turf at all (St. Johns County LDC), but ask the county about your parcel before you settle the layout.

faq.q: Is there a rebate for replacing my lawn with turf?
faq.a: No. St. Johns County, JEA and the St. Johns River Water Management District offer no rebate for artificial turf. What you save is the watering day, the fertilizer and the mowing.
